To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the lack of standard procedure to guide the eHealth systems lifecycle across the health sector is a key issue which hinders the realization of the benefits of ICT use in health sector in Tanzania and the willingness to collaboration is still poor.

The lack of a standard procedure to guide the eHealth lifecycle and poor collaboration between stakeholders in the health sector are the key issues which hampers interoperability and thus the manifestation of benefits of ICT use in Tanzania.

the lack of standardization of eHealth systems, poor collaboration among stakeholders and lack of a national strategy to guide the implementation of eHealth systems are the key issues which hampers the manifestation of the benefits of ICT use in Tanzania health care systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to improve the current eHealth landscape in Tanzania.
understanding the eHealth landscape and the challenges of interoperability and collaboration in Tanzania.
the identification of the challenges of interoperability and collaboration among health sector stakeholders and to provide recommendations to improve the current situation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current eHealth implementations are not interoperable and collaboration among health stakeholders is poor.
the current e-health implementations in Tanzania are fragmented, not interoperable and collaboration between health stakeholders is still limited.

, the eHealth systems in Tanzania are still in the early stage of development and there is a need for a more comprehensive and integrated approach to the implementation of eHealth systems in the country.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is a need to establish a national eHealth architecture which will guide the implementation of eHealth systems and services across the health sector in Tanzania.
the health sector of the country is still far from realizing the benefits of ICT use and the e-health implementations.
the current eHealth solutions in Tanzania are not well interoperable.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, the Tanzanian health sector needs to adopt an approach to guide the lifecycle and management of eHealth systems.
, there is need for the development of a framework for e-health interoperability and collaboration which will guide all stakeholders in Tanzania to ensure the realization of the benefits of e-health.
, the current eHealth landscape in Tanzania has not yet reached the level of maturity where it can provide the desired benefits.
